ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that point $O$ is the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$, with $\angle A=35^\circ$. By connecting $BO$ and $CO$, what is the measure of $\angle OBC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point O is the circumcenter of $\triangle ABC$ and $\angle A=35^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle BOC=2\angle A=70^\circ$, and BO=OC,

$\therefore \angle OBC=(180^\circ-\angle BOC)\div 2$,

$\therefore \angle OBC=\boxed{55^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, with A above, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right. Point O is located inside the triangle, and BO and CO have been connected. What is required is the angle ∠OBC at point B in triangle BOC. Reasoning: The problem gives that O is the circumcenter of △ABC, and ∠A = 35°. ∠BAC is an inscribed angle, and it subtends arc BC; ∠BOC is the central angle subtending the same arc BC, so ∠BOC = 2∠A = 70°. Also because O is the circumcenter, OB and OC are both radii of the circumcircle, OB = OC, and △BOC is an isosceles triangle. Therefore the two base angles are equal, ∠OBC = (180° - 70°)/2 = 55°.
